headline: Oxford Economics report: high cigarette taxation linked to expansion of illicit trade and billions in budget losses
summary: A new Oxford Economics study finds that excessive cigarette taxation is correlated with significant increases in illicit trade and billions in losses to the state budget. The report was covered in Romania.
why: Excise tax policy directly affects government revenue and the size of the illicit tobacco market. Tobacco companies are affected when tax changes shift consumer demand toward cheaper or illegal products.
